newsitem.title: JORDAN: Opposition group says it's back inside Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Opposition group says it's back inside Iraq.

text.p: An exiled Iraqi opposition group said on Saturday it had reestablished a presence in northern Iraq and had met Kurdish faction leaders to coordinate efforts to topple Iraqi President Saddam Hussein.
The Iraqi National Accord said in a statement it had also sent delegations to Iraq's neighbours Turkey and Iran as well as unnamed Arab countries to revive international links.
"The movement has succeeded in redeploying in northern Iraq, opening new bases in the towns and villages in the liberated areas of Iraqi Kurdistan," INA said in a statement.

INA officials in Amman were not immediately available to comment on the statement, which quoted a London-based spokesman. Most members of the movement, which set up offices in Jordan a year ago, divide their time between London and Amman.

Organised opposition to Saddam suffered a major setback last September when the Iraqi leader sent troops into northern Iraq in support of the rebel Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) against its rival Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK).
INA said its leaders had met both KDP and PUK members to discuss "the need to mobilise efforts to escalate the struggle against the Saddam regime."

Until last September Iraq's northern Kurdish provinces, patrolled by Western fighter jets since Iraq's 1991 Gulf War defeat, had gained a degree of autonomy from Baghdad. Two leading military defectors from Baghdad escaped into Turkey last year via northern Iraq.
